name: Judgement
upright: Independent eyes test the controls, findings rise into the light, and every exception is fixed, accepted or explained.
reversed: Testing without permission, scans passed off as pen tests, findings buried instead of fixed: judgment deferred, not escaped.
vision: An angel's trumpet sounds over a lake of open coffins, and three banners unfurl from its bell: a ledger page, a sealed letter handed only to those who ask, and a poster nailed up for the whole village. One rising figure is painted in a single instant; another must keep standing through a whole season of blasts. A clerk taps every coffin lid and notes the loose ones, while a masked figure holding a signed scroll pries them open. One figure climbs out through the coffin's floor. From the distant mountains a traveler spots a crack in the trumpet and whispers it to the angel alone, long before telling the crowd.
decode: Ledger page, sealed letter, village poster → SOC 1 covers financial reporting controls; SOC 2, security controls for restricted readers; SOC 3, a public summary.
Painted in an instant vs standing a season → Type I judges control design at a point in time; Type II tests operating effectiveness over a period.
The clerk tapping lids; the masked figure with a signed scroll → vulnerability scans find weaknesses; pen tests exploit them, only with written authorization.
Climbing out through the coffin's floor → misuse case testing: test what an attacker would try, not just the intended path.
The traveler whispering the crack to the angel first → ethical disclosure: tell the vendor privately and allow time to fix before going public.
facts: Internal audits use the organization's own staff; external audits bring an outside firm's independence; third-party audits are run for another party, such as a customer.
Test coverage = use cases tested ÷ total use cases. It can be measured by branch, condition, function, loop or statement coverage.
Static testing analyzes code without running it; dynamic testing exercises it while it runs; fuzzing feeds malformed input to expose crashes and flaws.
trap: The collective once accepted a Type I report as proof the controls work. Type I shows design on a single day; only Type II tests operation over months. Need the detail? SOC 2, not the public SOC 3.
